results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 63 body units align in spec order (p01 to p62, including p07a, p09a, p35b, p48a); every outline summary matches the controlling idea of its aligned spec paragraph; the three introduction callouts match nothing and are not prose units.
The reverse outline, written without the spec, lists the spec's controlling ideas in the spec's order; structure.json reports sections, unit counts and forms match.
The outliner marked no unit as holding two ideas.

Every unit ties to a supporting claim: scene to S2/S3, product model to S1, ownership to S2, choices/trade-offs/stages to S4 (and S1), PIM section and In Practice to S2/S3, failures to S5, conclusion to the thesis as a whole.

Each table, figure and quotation is followed or framed by a sentence saying what it shows (e.g. 'The table below is industry-typical, not a law'; 'These are vendor pages; none gives a testable threshold'; 'The setting carries out the ownership decision; it cannot make it'; 'Every one of these is a rule that changes on the channel's schedule').

Each boundary expresses the declared relationship and picks up the declared known information (e.g. 'Each of these pieces is written by someone', 'Kestrel & Pine's content row needs an owner', 'Once the test says a PIM is needed', 'W3, from the opening scene, is a bought PIM working by these three rules', 'Even with an owner in place'). The taxonomy paragraph opens with a parallel definition under the attributes-and-taxonomies subheading, which carries the additional-support relationship.

results.quote: Content is the slowest-changing fact on a product page (content, price, discount, stock), so it does not come first for its speed.
results.finding: Both flow readers had to re-read this sentence: the parenthetical repeats 'content' inside a sentence about content, and the negated reason ('does not come first for its speed') answers a claim nobody made. The next sentence gives the real reason; this one should be cut or rewritten to state it directly.

results.quote: Kestrel & Pine crossed the line around 2021–2022, when it added marketplaces (2021) and a third country (2022) to a Belgian storefront that already ran in two languages.
results.finding: Both flow readers stopped here: the chapter has presented Kestrel & Pine as selling in the Netherlands, Belgium and Germany with a Dutch description first, so 'a Belgian storefront that already ran in two languages' as the base reads as a new and conflicting fact, and the 'third country' is not named. The sentence should name the storefronts that existed before 2021 and that the third country was Germany.

results.quote: The count of producers and consumers decides, not revenue or the stage.
results.finding: Flow reader A had to reconcile three passages: K&P crossed the PIM line in 2021–2022 (the Growing stage in the stage table), the ownership table gives content to 'the shop platform at the Starting and Growing stages', and the stage section says the rule changes 'at the Growing-to-Omnichannel boundary'. They can be squared (the stage is typical, the count decides), but the text does not say so where the tension arises.

results.quote: It is right under the conditions the next table makes explicit, and the Giant's Boots when they do not hold.
results.finding: Flow reader B looked for the conditions in the trade-off table and found the explicit producer-and-consumer test only in the recommendation paragraph after it; the pointer should name where the test is stated.

results.quote: One buyable combination of option values: size M, color moss
results.finding: 'Option value' (on the does_not_know list) is used in the table one paragraph before it is defined ('an option value is one choice (M)'). The example makes it clear; negligible. Not reported by a flow reader, and the draft does define it.
The introduction opens with a concrete case (the Ridgewalker's 24 variants and a correction that reaches one channel), states the claim and gives a roadmap; none of the weak patterns.

The conclusion opens from the failures section, returns to the opening case, synthesizes the three rules as one design and sorts the take-aways by how settled they are; no new subtopic, no 'in conclusion', no rephrased thesis alone.

It states what no section states alone (identifiers, one owner per attribute and the route back are one design; a PIM keeps the second and third only when several teams write and several channels read) and why it matters ('a PIM bought without the table becomes a fifth copy with a login').
'The chapter opened with a corrected waterproof rating that reaches the web shop and not the marketplace: that happens because no system owns the rating.' returns to callback.to.

The intro-only reader predicted the opening case, the product model and ownership, the four arrangements with trade-offs, the PIM test and scale stages, how the pieces fit with a PIM, the channels' rules, Kestrel & Pine's decision and the failures, in the body's order, with Kestrel & Pine's season launch and platform, channel and standards documentation as evidence, and the tone. Matches expected in substance (expected lists the PIM before the choices, the spec's earlier order; the reader follows the current roadmap).

The reader answers 'should not buy', applies the test of more than one producing team and more than one consuming channel ('The count of producers and consumers decides, not revenue or the stage'), says the shop platform is right below the line and names the Giant's Boots. Matches expected.

The reader says no system owns the rating, that the correction belongs in the owning system (the PIM) from which the web shop and the marketplace both receive it, and that the shop platform's editor is read-only for fields it does not own. Matches expected.
The reader says retire the SKU, issue a new one and map the old one for history, never correct in place and never reuse, because orders, warehouses and marketplaces are keyed on it. Matches expected.
